facts.fact: The guide states that the TV screen viewers watch CTV ads on is typically 50 or more inches.
The guide says viewers have about 3 seconds before they mentally check out during a commercial break, so the opening must hook them quickly.
facts.quote: You have about 3 seconds before viewers mentally check out during a commercial break.

facts.fact: The guide recommends including the business name or logo in the first 5 seconds of a CTV ad.
facts.quote: Include your name/logo in the first 5 seconds

facts.fact: The guide recommends saying the brand name aloud at least twice in a CTV ad.
facts.quote: Say your name aloud at least twice

facts.fact: The guide recommends running each test version of a CTV ad for 2 to 4 weeks before reviewing performance data.
The guide lists standard CTV ad length as 15 or 30 seconds, and says 30 seconds is the most common.
facts.quote: Length:** 15 or 30 seconds (30 is most common)

facts.fact: The guide lists 1920x1080 (1080p HD) as the minimum resolution for standard CTV ad specs.
The guide lists 16:9 as the standard aspect ratio for CTV ads.
The guide lists 24, 25, or 30 frames per second as the standard frame rates for CTV ads.
The guide lists MP4 or MOV as the standard file formats for CTV ads.
The page states that 30 seconds is the standard and most effective length for CTV advertising.
facts.quote: 30 seconds is the standard and most effective length for CTV advertising.

facts.fact: The page says 15-second CTV ads work for simple awareness messages.
facts.quote: 15-second ads work for simple awareness messages, while 60-second spots are reserved for complex stories.

facts.fact: The page says 60-second CTV spots are reserved for complex stories.
facts.quote: while 60-second spots are reserved for complex stories.
